questions.q: What protocol does HTTP typically ride on top of?
options: UDP
TCP
DHCP
DNS
questions.explain: HTTP relies on TCP's reliable, ordered delivery, so the three-way handshake happens before any HTTP request is sent.

questions.q: Which HTTP method is used to create a new resource, such as submitting a new order?
options: GET
DELETE
POST
PATCH
questions.explain: POST is the method used to create something new, like submitting a new order on a checkout form.

questions.q: What does an HTTP status code of 404 indicate?
options: The request succeeded
The server itself encountered an error
Nothing exists at the requested path
The client should look somewhere else for the resource
questions.explain: A 404 status code means the server could not find anything at the requested path.

questions.q: What does HTTPS add on top of plain HTTP?
options: A completely different set of methods and status codes
An encrypted TLS tunnel wrapping the same request-response exchange
A faster, connectionless version of the same protocol
Automatic retries for failed requests
questions.explain: HTTPS sends the exact same HTTP methods and status codes, but wraps the whole exchange in an encrypted TLS tunnel so it can't be read in transit.

questions.q: Why must a checkout or login form always use HTTPS instead of plain HTTP?
options: Plain HTTP cannot carry form data at all
Plain HTTP sends everything as readable text, so anyone intercepting the traffic could read submitted data like passwords
HTTPS is required only for pages with images
Plain HTTP uses a different, incompatible set of status codes
questions.explain: Plain HTTP traffic is unencrypted and readable by anyone positioned between the client and server; HTTPS encrypts it so sensitive data like passwords can't be read in transit.
